question:
**Given below are four sentences which are jumbled. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. Schools are closed for the Christmas and winter break at this time of the year.

B. Christmas and New Year are the time of the year to celebrate.

C. All over the city, winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars lend fun and warmth in the cold.

D. For the second time in a row, we are likely to see restrained celebrations for fear of the pandemic raising its ugly head again.
solution:
The correct answer is '**BACD**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• **Sentence B** will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence that tells us about Christmas and New Year.
 
• **Sentence A** will be the next sentence because it further tells us that schools are closed during this time.
 
• **Sentence C** will be the next sentence because it tells us that winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars can be seen during this time.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence D** will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **B**: Christmas and New Year are the time of the year to celebrate.
 
• **A**: Schools are closed for the Christmas and winter break at this time of the year.
 
• **C**: All over the city, winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars lend fun and warmth in the cold.
 
• **D**: For the second time in a row, we are likely to see restrained celebrations for fear of the pandemic raising its ugly head again.

 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** ***(B).** Christmas and New Year are the time of the year to celebrate.** (A).** Schools are closed for the Christmas and winter break at this time of the year. **(C). **All over the city, winter carnivals and Christmas bazaars lend fun and warmth in the cold. **(D).** For the second time in a row, we are likely to see restrained celebrations for fear of the pandemic raising its ugly head again.*
